messages:
perf-bot: nightly alert — p95 latency increased 28% for model=llama-7b-quant on pool=gpu-t4-dedicated, starting ~2026-03-15T02:45Z

alex: I see it on the dashboard. Latency drift starts around 02:30 and spikes at 02:50. Canary rollout windows show activity 02:10-02:40.

maria: which change went live around that time? We merged the kernel-selector refactor + batching tweaks yesterday evening.

alex: rollout id r-2026-03-15-2 (canary).

ci-bot: CI perf run failed: suite="runtime/kv_throughput" throughput -34% vs baseline on main.

tyler: starting a bisect against the recent merges. Command used:
```

git bisect start --bad HEAD --good v2026-03-01
# run perf harness iteratively
```

jamie: uploaded a flamegraph from the canary pod at 02:50 — quick top of stack:
```
flamegraph top:
  36% runtime::kernel_dispatch
  22% kernel::int8_matmul
  11% kv_cache::lookup
   9% kv_cache::rehash
```

jamie: kv_cache::rehash is unusually hot — we see far more rehash work than in baseline captures.

maria: recall we switched cache fingerprinting to xxh3 in the kernel-selector PR to speed key comparisons. That could change bucket distribution and trigger rehashes.

rupert: also batching heuristic changed: we attempted to prioritize micro-batches for latency. Logs show many simultaneous small batches leading to contention on the KV structures. Two orthogonal changes landed together.

alex: hypothesis: micro-batching increases concurrent KV insert/resize pressure + new hash function alters load factor behaviour -> more rehashing -> CPU/latency spike.

tyler: bisect points to commit a3f4b2c (merge that combined kernel-selector, batching refactor, and hash change). I'll split pieces to find the primary culprit.

maria: quick experiment: revert the batching heuristic locally and run the perf harness for 10 minutes:
```
./perf_harness --model=llama-7b-quant --workload=mixed_short --duration=600
# result: p95 returns to baseline within noise
```

jamie: confirmed on staging: reverting batching brings p95 down, though int8 kernel still shows ~5% more CPU for some shapes but not enough to explain 28% latency increase.

rupert: CI failure aligns — kv_throughput drop is sensitive to batch shape distribution. Micro-batches increased per-token overhead and triggered rehashing thrash.

alex: we should pause the rollout until we have a remediation. I don't want more customers on canary hitting this.

maria: proposed patch: keep micro-batching opt-in but add two mitigations — 1) sticky batching for requests with identical key prefixes for 50ms to preserve batch locality; 2) restore legacy hash for this release while we tune xxh3 params.

tyler: opening PR with the batching patch + perf runs: PR #2489. Initial CI perf run shows p95 improved but still -6% vs baseline. More tuning incoming.

jamie: attaching flamegraphs and KV metrics to PR. Also shared local repro steps for flame capture:
```
RUNTIME_PROFILE=1 ./runtime --model=llama-7b-quant --sequence-distribution=small --threads=16
# then process with perf-map + flamegraph scripts
```

rupert: I'll run microbench comparing xxh3 vs legacy hash on insertion/rehash paths to quantify cost per-op and rehash frequency.

alex: action items:
- tyler: land batching patch and rerun perf (#2489) -> in progress
- jamie: attach flamegraphs + kv metrics -> in progress
- rupert: run hash microbench -> assigned
- maria: prep revert-ready branch if patch misses EOD -> assigned
- alex: paused rollout r-2026-03-15-2 and notified support/infra -> done

maria: if the patch doesn't get us within threshold, we'll revert the combined merge and ship kernel-selector changes separately after we stabilize KV behavior.

tyler: noted. Running extended perf run overnight once PR updates land.

alex: thanks — hold canary and notify PM/support. We'll reconvene after the next perf results. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: alert acknowledged. Canary r-2026-03-15-2 status: HOLD.
